newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S. Korea doubles Dec jet/kerosene imports over Nov.
newsitem.headline: S. Korea doubles Dec jet/kerosene imports over Nov.

text.p: South Korea has almost doubled its December jet/kerosene purchases over November due the delayed startup of one crude unit and the impending energy deregulation which starts in 1997, industry sources in Seoul said on Friday.
Sources estimated South Korea bought eight to ten 30,000-35,000-tonne cargoes on a spot basis in December, up from about five in November.
"December purchases have almost doubled over November," one source said.
Traders said at least one other refiner is still in the market looking to buy a December cargo.
The rise in imports are due partly to the deregulation of the South Korean oil industry whereby product prices and oil imports and exports will be liberalised from January 1, 1997.
Sources said the delay in the startup of LG-Caltex Oil Corp's 220,000 barrels per day (bpd) crude distillation unit to late December, also contributed to increased imports.

The unit which is capable of processing 270,000 bpd of crude is expected to reach maximum output by late December, the company said.

South Korea's most recent purchases were made earlier this week when two refiners bought one cargo each of jet/kerosene at a premium of between $1.70-1.80 per barrel to spot Singapore quotes, on a cost-and-freight basis, traders said.
Jet/kerosene prices in Singapore have risen sharply over the past few weeks due to the increased demand from South Korea and Japan for December cargoes.
Late last week early December jet fuel traded at a new post winter high of $32.30 per barrel on a free-on-board Singapore basis.
But South Korea is not likely to buy as much of the heating fuel in January as the refiners are said to have built up healthy inventories, sources said.
According to the Korea Petroleum Development Corp, kerosene stocks at the end of September were at 8.297 million barrels, up sharply from the 5.77 million barrels in August.
